question: A potassium hydroxide preparation is conducted on a skin scraping of the hypopigmented area. Microscopy of the preparation shows long hyphae among clusters of yeast cells. Based on these findings, which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Skin scraping shows long hyphae among clusters of yeast cells -> Suggestive of dermatophyte infection -> Treat with antifungal medication -> Topical antifungals are usually effective for localized infections -> Topical nystatin is commonly used for yeast infections -> Topical nystatin is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy in this case -> 95%
analysis: The presence of long hyphae among clusters of yeast cells on microscopy suggests a fungal infection, most likely a dermatophyte infection. The most appropriate pharmacotherapy for dermatophyte infections is oral ketoconazole.
